column1: # One row per real NXP MCUXpresso SDK example we run on the model. The scorecard
# generator (tools/scorecard.sh) runs each row and MEASURES the verdict against
# an EXTERNAL oracle -- a string the NXP firmware itself prints on success, cited
# by SDK file:line in the `oracle_src` column. The oracle is SOURCED from NXP's
# code, never from our model: that is the whole point (see docs/validation/README.md).
#   tier      A = prebuilt cm33 .bin from the SDK zip (no toolchain needed)
#             B = built from source (needs SDK_ROOT + VENV + arm-none-eabi-gcc)
#   example   Tier A: demo path as it appears in the prebuilt tree.
#   kind      pass   console MUST contain <oracle>            -> PASS / FAIL
#             banner console MUST contain <oracle> (start banner); the example
#                    then needs an external HOST to complete  -> BANNER (blocked)
#             xfail  <oracle> is the SUCCESS string it does NOT reach; a known,
#             value  no console oracle; proven by a dedicated value-test (note)
#             xbuild build unsupported for this board in this SDK (note = reason)
#   oracle    the external success/banner string (SOURCED). '-' if none.
#   oracle_src  SDK file:line the oracle came from, or how it was established.
#   note      human note / what blocks / which value-test proves it.
# EXPECTED_ROWS is asserted by the generator (coverage gate). If you add or remove
# a row you MUST bump EXPECTED_A / EXPECTED_B in tools/scorecard.sh, or the gate
# FAILS -- a silent drop must never read as "everything covered".
